title: What is known about 1RB0RA_0LC0RF_0LB1RD_1LE---_1RA0LF_1LE0RC
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0RA_0LC0RF_0LB1RD_1LE---_1RA0LF_1LE0RC.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. The two long passes of an excursion over the 11010 block are proved in Lean for every block length (kernel). In between, the head works on a counter whose digits and carry rule are not decoded yet. The C simulator runs 1011 steps without a halt.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (D1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: The two passes, for all lengths
claims.text: pass_left: from L 1 1 0 0 0 1 1 0 1 0 (11010)^(n+2) B> 0^∞ the head crosses the block to the counter in 17n + 54 steps. pass_right: from L A> 1 1 1 0 (11010)^(n+1) 0^∞ it crosses back to a new cell at the right end in 27n + 44 steps. Both hold for every n and every tape L.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>11</sup> steps
claims.text: A direct C simulation runs 10<sup>11</sup> steps without a halt; the tape is then 202,789 cells wide.

claims.title: One word per excursion, a counter on the left
claims.text: Each excursion lengthens the 11010 block by one word (961, 962, … at 3·107 steps, 6,038 at 109). The head turns inside the counter at depths in classes 25 cells apart, each class about 2.6 times rarer than the one before, the signature of a counter with 25-cell digits. Every digit has the form 11a0 11b0 1100 110c 0 11d0 11e0: five bits, 28 of the 32 patterns seen. The first 1,260 cells of the tape are the same at steps 3·107 and 109.

claims.title: Size of the tape description (family screen)
claims.text: At the 4 records between 2.6·10<sup>8</sup> and 1.6·10<sup>10</sup> steps (first new leftmost or rightmost cell after each threshold 10<sup>6</sup>·4^k) the tape has 17,894 to 137,409 visited cells and compresses to 117 to 147 level-2 tokens (repeats of a word of at most 40 cells, then repeats of groups of such tokens).

claims.title: Proposed family: F06, block-list counters
claims.text: This machine has the table of 1RB---_1LC0RF_1LD0LC_0RE0LF_0RD1LA_1RB0LE read in a mirror with the states renamed (related.json), started in another state. On the screen the two runs have the same numbers within a few cells at every record (for example 137,409 and 137,401 visited cells at 1.6·1010 steps, a block of 27,165 five-cell words in both and 32 copies of a 25-cell word in both). That is an observation at the sampled records, not a proof that the two runs correspond. The description does not grow during the present epoch: 117 to 147 level-2 tokens at the four right-end records from 2.6·108 to 1.6·1010 steps, and 306 to 314 runs in the macro simulator (blocks of 5 cells) at 80 sampled right-end records from 3·107 to 1016 steps. Only the block (11010)^k grows. The counter in the wall, with its five free cells per 25-cell digit, is described above; the sister's page has the periods 8, 64 and 512 of its first digits and the one overflow seen so far (between steps 1.4·106 and 4.5·106 in the sister's run). A counter that is rebuilt when it overflows belongs with the counter families (F06), not with the bounded engines (F01).

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. It halts exactly when C reads a 1 with a 1 on its right. The passes never do this; the counter work between them is not a closed rule yet.

claims.title: Related holdouts
claims.text: The same table as 1RB---_1LC0RF_1LD0LC_0RE0LF_0RD1LA_1RB0LE up to renaming and mirroring, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows yet. This machine keeps a counter near the left of its tape and a long, growing block of 11010 words to its right. Each visit to the counter ticks it and adds one word to the block. It has run 1011 steps without stopping.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator.

sections.heading: Which family it belongs to
html: The 22 machines of family F09 (“bouncers over lists of counters, not yet classified”) were screened in one way. The machine runs from blank tape for 2·1010 steps; each time the tape reaches a new cell after a threshold, the tape is compressed twice: first repeats of one word, then repeats of groups of words. If the tape is a few growing blocks and a bounded rest, the number of level-2 tokens stays bounded while the tape grows. Everything in this section is observed in one run. None of it is proved.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.493).
After 109 steps the tape spans 34,618 cells (204 left of the start, 25,373 right), with a density of 1s of 0.599.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: What the tape is made of
html: After a while the tape has three parts: a stretch of the word P = 11000110 on the left, a counter of about 1,500 cells built from the words 1100, 1110, 11010 and P 0, and then, after a fixed marker P 0 0 P 1 0, a long uniform block of q = 11010 (accent colour). The head starts each excursion in state B on the blank cell at the right end.

sections.heading: One excursion
html:
1. Left pass: the head runs left across the whole block, 17 steps per word (pass_left).
  2. Counter work: it bounces in the low end of the counter for a few thousand steps and rewrites a few hundred cells there.
  3. Right pass: it runs back across the block, 27 steps per word (pass_right), and the block is one word longer.
So the k-th excursion costs about 44k steps, and the tape grows like the square root of the time.

sections.heading: A counter with long digits
html: How far into the counter the head goes changes from excursion to excursion in a ruler-like way. Between steps 3·107 and 109 the deepest cell of each return falls into classes 25 cells apart:

leftmost cell12991274–821249–571224–321199–12071174–821149–571124–32≤ 1107
returns3522,6801,5686482499135139

Each class is about 2.6 times rarer than the one before: a counter whose digits are about 25 cells long, with a carry reaching digit j about once every 2.6j excursions. Each digit has the form 11a0 11b0 1100 110c 0 11d0 11e0, five bits a to e; 28 of the 32 patterns occur. What one visit does to the bits, and so the exact growth factor, is not decoded yet.

sections.heading: Where it could halt
html: The only halting transition is D reading 1, and D is entered only when C reads a 1 and moves right. So the machine halts exactly when C reads a 1 with another 1 on its right. The two passes never do this (proved for all lengths); whether the counter work ever does is the open part.

sections.heading: What is proved
html:
• Kernel: pass_left and pass_right for all block lengths (lean/Rules.lean); no halt in 10,000 steps.
  • native_decide: no halt in 107 steps.
  • Trusted computation: no halt in 1011 steps.
  • Open: whether it ever halts.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machine below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in the other, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.

  • 1RB---_1LC0RF_1LD0LC_0RE0LF_0RD1LA_1RB0LE: rename A→C, B→D, C→E, D→A, E→B, F→F and exchange left and right; it is this table started in state D, in a mirror

summary: A counter of about 1,500 cells sits at the left while a block of 11010 words grows on its right, one word per excursion; each excursion crosses the block, works on the low digits of the counter and crosses back. The two passes are proved in Lean.
